title: Cancellation of a shifted Tate line in the canonical double-Hom map
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, integers $a,n\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme in its domain, and use the actual coefficient categories, tensor and internal Hom of [sk-def-sf-operations](i). Write $\mathbf1=\Lambda_X$, $H(P,M)=R\mathcal Hom_X(P,M)$ and $P^\vee=H(P,\mathbf1)$. The integral unit and tensor are completed; the field categories are the specified rationalization and common finite-stage categories, respectively. All tensor constraints and symmetries below are those of these categories, including their cohomological signs.

Let $m,r\in\mathbf Z$, put $L=\Lambda_X(m)[2r]$ and $L^{-1}=\Lambda_X(-m)[-2r]$ with their opposite-line evaluation identifications, and let $\gamma:L\xrightarrow{\sim}W$ be any isomorphism. Write $D_WP=H(P,W)$. Let $P\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect and let $c_{P,L}:P^\vee\otimes L\to H(P,L)$ be the transpose of coefficient evaluation tensored with $L$ (with symmetry moving $L$ past $P$). Assume this comparison is invertible, and set $\theta_P=c_{P,L}^{-1}H(P,\gamma^{-1})$.

For every object $U$, let
$$q_U:H(U\otimes L,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(U,\mathbf1)$$
be the composite of $H(1_{U\otimes L},\lambda_L^{-1}):H(U\otimes L,L)\to H(U\otimes L,\mathbf1\otimes L)$, where $\lambda_L:\mathbf1\otimes L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ is the left unitor, with the canonical cancellation isomorphism $c_{U,\mathbf1,L}=s_{U,\mathbf1,L}^{-1}:H(U\otimes L,\mathbf1\otimes L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(U,\mathbf1)$ of [lem-sf-invertible-factor-hom-cancellation], applied in the closed symmetric monoidal structure of [sk-def-sf-operations](i) to the invertible factor $J=L$ with $I=L^{-1}$. Thus $q_U$ is natural in $U$, and $q_U^{-1}$ is the transpose of coefficient evaluation $H(U,\mathbf1)\otimes U\to\mathbf1$ tensored with $L$, followed by $\lambda_L$. On morphisms out of every test object $V$, after the tensor--Hom adjunction, $q_U^{-1}$ is the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(V\otimes U,\mathbf1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(V\otimes U\otimes L,L)$ sending $v$ to $v\otimes1_L$ (with $\lambda_L$).

Define $t_P=H(\theta_P^{-1},\gamma^{-1}):D_WD_WP\xrightarrow{\sim}H(P^\vee\otimes L,L)$. Let $\delta^W_P:P\to D_WD_WP$ and $j_P:P\to P^{\vee\vee}$ be the transposes of the respective evaluations after interchanging their tensor factors by the symmetry. Then the equation of canonical maps is
$$q_{P^\vee}\circ t_P\circ\delta^W_P=j_P.$$
The internal-Hom isomorphism and this equality use the signed derived symmetry; no unsigned identification on cohomology is substituted for them. No smooth morphism, absolute dualizing object, or general geometric biduality theorem is assumed.

proof.text: Use the supplied right-tensor adjunction of the actual coefficient closed structure. Its counit and Hom equivalence give uncurry(g)=tensor(g,1) followed by evaluation. Adjunction naturality in the test object and target, together with evaluation_naturality in the source, gives uncurry(g followed by H(f,h))=tensor(1,f) followed by uncurry(g) followed by h. Apply these formulas to orientedHomCancellationInverse to obtain its explicit uncurry: inverse associator followed by tensor(uncurry(g),1_L) followed by the left unitor. Tensoring on the right by L is an equivalence by the existing source theorem tensorRightEquivalenceOfTensorIso(a,b); its fully faithful Hom map, the adjunction bijections and the invertible associator and unitor show that postcomposition with this exact cancellation inverse is bijective for every test object, using [lem-sf-quasi-inverse-hom-bijection]. Thus it is an isomorphism by isIso_of_yoneda_map_bijective. Set q to the inverse of its asIso. This works with arbitrary two-sided inverse identifications a and b; no triangle compatibility is assumed.

proof.text: Uncurry the naturality square for the explicit cancellation inverse. Evaluation source naturality and associator middle naturality identify both sides. Multiply by the inverse isomorphisms to get the required naturality of q. The uncurry formula of step 1 proves the exact test-object transpose equation. The composite of transpose, postcomposition by q inverse, and inverse transpose is an equivalence of Hom sets, hence the displayed map on test-object Hom sets is bijective. All these are direct calculations in the supplied adjunction.

source.place: Tags 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible) and 0GWJ (categories-remark-internal-hom-monoidal); explicit expansion of main-20261015 sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect proof sentence 4.

proof.text: Put A=H(P,1) and theta=orientedHomThetaInverse(P,L,W,gamma). The first evaluation law of [lem-sf-coefficient-evaluation-naturality] identifies the uncurry of the actual ringedSiteDualEvaluationLeft(P,L). Apply the uncurry map law to its composite with H(1,gamma.hom). Since theta.hom is precisely this composite, its evaluation is associator(A,L,P), then tensor(1_A,symmetry(L,P)), then inverse associator(A,P,L), then tensor(evaluation(P,1),1_L), then the left unitor and gamma.hom. This proves the needed conditional evaluation equation directly, retaining the explicit comparison-invertibility instance.

source.place: Tags 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible) and 0GWJ (categories-remark-internal-hom-monoidal); explicit expansion of main-20261015 sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect proof sentence 4.

proof.text: Cancel q_A inverse on the right of the desired bidual equality. The remaining equation is delta_W followed by H(theta.hom,gamma.inv) equals j followed by the explicit cancellation inverse. Apply injectivity of inverse transpose. The uncurry map law and the definition of ringedSiteBidual rewrite the left side as tensor(1_P,theta.hom), then symmetry(P,H(P,W)), evaluation(P,W), and gamma.inv. Braiding naturality moves theta.hom before evaluation. Substitute the evaluation equation of step 3; gamma.hom followed by gamma.inv cancels.

source.place: Tags 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible) and 0GWJ (categories-remark-internal-hom-monoidal); explicit expansion of main-20261015 sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect proof sentence 4.

proof.text: Expand symmetry(P,A tensor L) with braiding_tensor_right_hom. Cancel inverse-associator/associator pairs and combine the whiskered crossings symmetry(P,L) and symmetry(L,P). SymmetricCategory.symmetry cancels these crossings. Associator coherence leaves inverse associator(P,A,L), then tensor(symmetry(P,A) followed by evaluation(P,1),1_L), then the left unitor. This is the uncurry of j followed by q inverse from step 1. Inverse transpose is injective, so the required equality follows. This uses the supplied signed symmetry throughout and does not require perfectness beyond the unchanged hypotheses.

The categorical argument works for every pair L,I with the supplied inverse isomorphisms, so the existing shifted-Tate object equalities need no transport and all four stated conclusions follow with their original hypotheses unchanged.
